checks.description: Rows that are byte-for-byte copies of an earlier row.
checks.rationale: Pure duplicates double-count shipments in route metrics; the copy carries no extra information.

checks.description: shipment_id appears more than once with differing field values.
checks.rationale: The primary key must be unique. Keep the most complete version (fewest blank fields, then first seen) and quarantine the others so the conflict can be investigated with the source system.

checks.description: shipment_id / customer_id / vessel_id do not match the expected SHP-#####, CUST-####, VSL-#### patterns.
checks.rationale: Malformed identifiers cannot be joined or looked up reliably.

checks.description: origin_port or destination_port is not present in ports.csv (e.g. XXTST, ZZZZZ, UNKNW).
checks.rationale: Placeholder / test port codes cannot be attributed to a real route; including them would create phantom routes in the stats endpoint and noise in the model.

checks.description: origin_port equals destination_port.
checks.rationale: A shipment cannot start and end at the same port in this domain.

checks.description: A non-blank timestamp column does not parse as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.
checks.rationale: Delay and transit calculations depend on every timestamp being valid.

checks.description: booking_date, planned_departure or planned_arrival is blank.
checks.rationale: Planned dates are required for delay calculation and are core model features.

checks.description: planned_arrival is on or before planned_departure, or planned_departure is before booking_date.
checks.rationale: An impossible plan makes planned transit time and the delay baseline meaningless.

checks.description: actual_departure is earlier than booking_date — the vessel left before the shipment was booked.
checks.rationale: The actual departure timestamp is impossible, so it is set to NULL (transit_days_actual becomes NULL) while actual_arrival — which looks plausible — is kept so the delay metric survives. Row is flagged.

checks.description: actual_arrival is on or before actual_departure.
checks.rationale: Impossible sequence; actual timestamps would be nulled and the row flagged.

checks.description: status is not one of ['CANCELLED', 'DELAYED', 'DELIVERED'] as written (e.g. 'delivered', 'Complete', 'COMPLETED').
checks.rationale: Case / synonym variants are normalised via an alias map. In the curated layer status is then re-derived from the actual timestamps so it can never disagree with the delay metric.

checks.description: status is blank or a placeholder such as 'N/A'.
checks.rationale: Status is re-derived from actual timestamps where possible; otherwise set to UNKNOWN and flagged.

checks.description: Status contradicts the actual timestamps: a non-cancelled shipment with no actual_arrival (e.g. 'COMPLETED' but never arrived), or a CANCELLED shipment that has an actual_arrival.
checks.rationale: These rows have no observed outcome. They are kept (status=UNKNOWN, delay NULL) so the shipment can still be looked up, but they are excluded from on-time metrics and from model training.

checks.description: cargo_type differs from the canonical spelling only by case or whitespace (e.g. 'FURNITURE', ' Chemicals').
checks.rationale: Unnormalised categories split one class into several, hurting both aggregates and one-hot features.

checks.description: cargo_type is blank.
checks.rationale: Kept with cargo_type='Unknown' — the row is otherwise valid and cargo type is not a key field.

checks.description: weight_tons is blank.
checks.rationale: Kept as NULL; the model imputes with the training median.

checks.description: weight_tons is zero or negative.
checks.rationale: Physically impossible. Set to NULL and flagged rather than dropping an otherwise valid shipment; taking abs() would be a guess.

checks.description: container_count is 0 (or negative).
checks.rationale: A booked shipment must carry at least one container. Set to NULL and flagged.

checks.description: container_count exceeds 100 (bulk of data is 1-50; outliers are 500-1000).
checks.rationale: Values an order of magnitude above the distribution look like unit / keying errors. Set to NULL and flagged so they don't dominate the model's numeric features.

checks.description: A reference field (name, country, region, timezone, congestion) is blank.
checks.rationale: Reference data is small and curated by hand: the missing country for BEANR (Antwerp) is filled with 'Belgium' from a documented fix list rather than dropping a port that 180+ shipments use.

checks.description: port_code appears more than once.
checks.rationale: Duplicate reference keys would fan out every join.

checks.description: avg_congestion_score is outside [0, 1] or not numeric.
checks.rationale: Score is used as a model feature and should be a normalised value.

checks.description: Rows that are exact copies of an earlier row (typical at-least-once delivery in a stream).
checks.rationale: Replayed events would double-count delay minutes.

checks.description: event_id is reused by events with different content (different port, vessel, timestamp).
checks.rationale: These are distinct events with a colliding ID, not replays. Both are kept and the curated layer uses a deterministic surrogate key (hash of all fields) so neither is lost.

checks.description: event_type is blank.
checks.rationale: An event without a type cannot be interpreted; quarantined for replay once the producer is fixed.

checks.description: event_type is non-blank but not one of ['ARRIVAL', 'BERTHED', 'CUSTOMS_CLEARED', 'DELAYED', 'DEPARTURE', 'INSPECTION', 'LOADING_COMPLETE'].
checks.rationale: Unknown event types would be silently ignored by downstream consumers.

checks.description: vessel_id is a placeholder / test value (VSL-0000, VSL-9999) that never appears in shipments.
checks.rationale: Events for test vessels would pollute port-level delay metrics.

checks.description: port_code is not present in ports.csv.
checks.rationale: Cannot be attributed to a known port.

checks.description: event_timestamp is blank or not YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.
checks.rationale: Events without a valid time cannot be ordered in the stream.

checks.description: delay_minutes is non-numeric, negative, or above 1440.
checks.rationale: Negative or multi-day per-event delays are almost certainly unit errors.

checks.description: event_type is DELAYED but delay_minutes is 0.
checks.rationale: Contradictory but harmless for current consumers; flagged so producers can be asked about it.

checks.description: notes is blank.
checks.rationale: Free-text notes are optional; kept as NULL.
